note: Capability registry: actions are DATA, not code. The encoder's action head is derived from these descriptions, so adding a capability means appending an entry and re-encoding it â€” no retraining, no new class id.

capabilities.description: Look up game knowledge (monsters, spells, quests, items, NPCs, achievements, dungeons) in the local DofusDB cache. Use before claiming any game fact.
capabilities.returns: list of compact records with 'id', 'name' (localised dict) and key fields

query.doc: Free-text name or keyword, any of the 4 languages.

capabilities.description: Travel to a target. Give one of: [x,y] coordinates, a zaap name, an NPC, a map id, a cell, or a direction. `direction` leaves by that edge; `cell` walks to that specific spot on the current map.
capabilities.returns: transition ack; for an adjacent map the client walks to the border cell first, and a non-adjacent target is refused with the current map's exits

npc_id.doc: NPC id on the current map, as listed in snapshot.map.npcs.

cell.doc: Walk to this cell on the current map (a specific spot).

direction.doc: Leave by this edge of the current map.

capabilities.description: Follow a character on the current map and through map changes. Empty name means 'follow the order giver'.
capabilities.returns: directive ack

name.doc: Character name to follow; empty = the order giver.

capabilities.description: List quests suitable for a level (and optionally an area), with start position and step objectives.
capabilities.returns: list of quests with id, localised name, level range and step objectives

area.doc: Area or subarea name filter, any language (e.g. 'astrub').

capabilities.description: Execute the next actionable step of a quest: navigate, talk to the NPC, harvest, or fight as the step objective requires.
capabilities.returns: per-step progress report

npc_id.doc: Talk to this NPC, by the template id the objective carries.

objective_id.doc: Validate this objective. Use it to claim one the game already accepts (objectiveStatus 2).

reply.doc: Which dialog reply to choose, by index. Defaults to 0, which is what an unanswered NPC dialog needs.

reply_text.doc: Which dialog reply to choose, by the exact French text reported in dialog.replies. With reply, both must agree.

close.doc: Close an open dialog whose reply list is empty.

accept.doc: Accept the quest this dialog is offering. The page sends QuestStartRequestMessage only when the dialog's own start_quest link matches quest_id, then closes.

capabilities.description: Start a farm loop: kill monster groups and/or harvest resources, looting according to the filter, optionally auto-selling.
capabilities.returns: farm session id and live counters

monster.doc: Monster id from the objective, or a name from the corpus. The client needs an id; the harness resolves a name.

resource.doc: Resource id from the objective, or a name. The client harvests the nearest interactive element; the id selects it when the client can.

zone.doc: Area/subarea to stay inside, any language.

loot_filter.doc: Item names to keep; others can be dropped.

auto_sell.doc: Auto-list kept loot on the market when bags fill.

capabilities.description: Stop the active farm loop and return to a safe idle state.
capabilities.returns: final farm counters

capabilities.description: Join a fight: a monster group containing the named monster, an explicit group, or the nearest group.
capabilities.returns: fight state

monster.doc: Monster id from the objective. The group containing it is chosen; the client knows which group that is.

group_id.doc: Explicit monster-group id, when the caller already has one.

capabilities.description: Pass the current combat turn.
capabilities.returns: ack

capabilities.description: List inventory contents, optionally filtered by kind.
capabilities.returns: items with id, name, quantity, unit weight

capabilities.description: Sell inventory items on the market (HDV) at a price rule. Default rule is median market price minus 1 kama.
capabilities.returns: per-item listing report (price used, quantity, market depth)

quantity.doc: Units to sell. Default 1: a bare "sell X" sells one unit, never the whole stack.

min_stock.doc: Keep at least this many units.

capabilities.description: Scan the market (HDV) for an item and return price statistics (min/median/max over current listings).
capabilities.returns: price stats and listing count

category.doc: Market category id, when browsing rather than searching.

capabilities.description: List an item for sale on the market at an explicit or rule-based price.
capabilities.returns: listing confirmations

capabilities.description: Send a chat message.
capabilities.returns: ack

capabilities.description: Request a structured snapshot of current game state (position, map, HP, inventory summary, active fight).
capabilities.returns: observation dict recorded into the trajectory log

capabilities.description: Emergency stop: halt farm/fight loops, stop acting, log out of dangerous situations. Always available.
capabilities.returns: ack

capabilities.description: Record something you discovered that the cache does not know (an NPC's map, a drop, a price, a quest prerequisite). Facts keep their provenance, so a wrong one can be corrected or forgotten. Never use this to copy the cache.
capabilities.returns: {'changed': bool, 'note': str}

value.doc: The fact as text or JSON, e.g. '12345' or '{"map": 123}'.

confidence.doc: 0-1; 0.9 if you saw it, 0.5 if inferred.

capabilities.description: Delete a fact that turned out to be wrong. Use it instead of storing a contradicting value, so the store stays small.
capabilities.returns: {'removed': bool}

key.doc: Key of the fact to remove.

reason.doc: Why it is wrong (kept in the log).

capabilities.description: Read the live combat board: turn owner, fighters, cells, HP/AP/MP, team membership, and the controlled character's spell descriptors. The result also carries a versioned observation and a contract naming any fact the client did not expose.
capabilities.returns: turn, fighter and spell facts from the live client, plus observation/contract

capabilities.description: Read the live board and compute this turn's legal move-and-cast plan: exact cell geometry, line of sight, AP/MP, cooldowns, resistances, damage and healing. top_k > 1 also returns alternative plans (including pass) for a ranker. Read-only; it never casts or moves anything. Every answer carries the live observation and its contract.
capabilities.returns: actions with cells/targets/AP/MP/damage, plus the normalized live observation, its contract, and the ranker decision

beam_width.doc: How many partial turns to keep while searching.

max_actions.doc: Maximum casts to consider in the plan.

top_k.doc: Also return this many candidate plans; 1 = best only.

rank_with_value.doc: Compatibility alias for ranker=value: rank candidates with the learned encounter value head.

ranker.doc: Which plan ranker to use. 'solver' keeps the solver order; 'value' ranks candidates with the learned value head and refuses when the live observation lacks self stats or enemy spell facts; 'grid' ranks with the 30M 560-cell solver-distillation model (opt-in, read-only, fails open when the artifact is absent).

capabilities.description: Estimate whether the controlled character can win a monster group visible on this map: turns to kill, incoming damage, expected HP loss, and a calibrated win probability. Read-only; it never joins or casts.
capabilities.returns: p_win (null until calibrated), raw_score, expected_hp_loss and turns, confidence, missing inputs, allowed and blocked_reason

monster.doc: Monster id or name. When several visible groups contain it, the least favourable one is estimated.

capabilities.description: Buy a market listing at or below a maximum unit price. uid is the listing id, not the item id. Use hdv.scan/hdv.prices first when only an item name or gid is known; the page resolves a listing only from prices the server already sent.
capabilities.returns: listing uid, quantity, unit price, total and price source

uid.doc: Market listing id (ExchangeBidHouseBuyMessage.uid), not the item id.

item.doc: Item name; used only to resolve an inventory-known gid.

gid.doc: Item generic id; used to find a cached listing.

max_price.doc: Maximum unit price. Required unless price is given; the handler never buys above it.

price.doc: Expected unit price; must be <= max_price when both are present.

capabilities.description: Equip or remove an item. A saved preset uses InventoryPresetUseMessage; object_uid uses the client's own inventory.equipItem path and reports which gate stopped it when it sends nothing. slot forces the client's ObjectSetPositionMessage for an item whose type blocks equipItem; remove (or slot -1) sends the same message with position -1, which is the only way to free a slot, since an occupied slot does not swap.
capabilities.returns: preset/object, post-state and the available presets

object_uid.doc: Inventory object UID; equips through the client's inventory.equipItem path.

slot.doc: Slot position ('weapon' or 0-16) sent via ObjectSetPositionMessage when equipItem sends nothing; -1 removes.

remove.doc: Send ObjectSetPositionMessage with position -1; alias of slot -1.

capabilities.description: Read or capture current market prices from the page's server-message price cache. This is a read-only observation, not a purchase.
capabilities.returns: average prices, cached listing statistics and cache ages

item.doc: Item name, when the page can resolve it from the inventory.

refresh.doc: Ask the server for the average-price table.

capabilities.description: Use a visible interactive element (door, chest, quest object, resource) through the client's own InteractiveUseRequestMessage.
capabilities.returns: chosen element id, skill instance uid and cell

cell.doc: Select the element standing on this cell.

name.doc: Reserved for a future named lookup; the page does not invent names it cannot read.

capabilities.description: Press the game's own UI: a menu-bar icon by name (Spell, Book, Map, Bag, Carac), any visible control by CSS selector, or a control the tutorial's hint/condition drives by object path (client_target: challenge, spell_upgrade_confirm, spell_plus, charac_update, world, and the later tutorials' controls: contextual_menu:N, npc_menu:N, trade_slot, trade_validate, craft_slot, craft_recipe, craft_merge, craft_drag, shop_category:N, shop_item:N, sell_info, bestiary_monster, bestiary_drop, close:NAME). The tutorial's interface steps are completed by this press; their objectives are server-counted and a claim on one ends the connection.
capabilities.returns: pressed selector, open windows before and after, and whether the press changed the open-window set

menu.doc: Menu icon name, e.g. Spell, Book, Map, Bag, Carac.

selector.doc: CSS selector for any other visible control, e.g. .shopBtn.

client_target.doc: Client-object control the tutorial points at: challenge, spell_upgrade_confirm, spell_plus, charac_update (spends unspent stat points, then fires the characteristics condition), world (a touchend on the game body for a TAP_ANYWHERE step), the later tutorials' controls (contextual_menu:N, npc_menu:N, trade_slot, trade_validate, craft_slot, craft_recipe, craft_merge, craft_drag, shop_category:N, shop_item:N, sell_info, bestiary_monster, bestiary_drop) or close:NAME (closes a window the step ends on closing).

close_first.doc: Window name to close before pressing, so the press produces a real opening.

cycle.doc: Press again after the window opens, so an open-and-close step is given back.

capabilities.description: List the menu-bar icons the client shows right now (key, disabled flag, position) and the open windows. Read-only.
capabilities.returns: icons list and open window names

capabilities.description: Buy the first article of the tutorial's shop window with the client's own hard-price button. The tutorial enables a fake shop whose purchase is free and whose button makes the client validate the quest objective itself; outside that mode the same button starts a real-currency purchase, so the page refuses and says so.
capabilities.returns: article id, the button pressed, open windows before/after

which.doc: Which article to buy; 'first' is the tutorial's pack.
